subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: After the branch is rebased cleanly, should OpenClaw accept leader-verified group kill as the default for omitted `detached` Unix cleanup?
rationale: The code fix is a plausible best fix for the gateway SIGTERM bug, but it changes shared process cleanup semantics for existing omitted-option callers and can trade accidental gateway termination for direct-PID fallback when leadership cannot be verified.

options.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup After Rebase
options.body: Resolve conflicts, preserve current-main behavior, and land the leader-check approach once focused tests and CI are clean.

options.title: Require More Caller State
options.body: Ask the contributor to carry explicit detached state through any additional owner-approved cleanup surfaces before accepting the helper default change.

options.title: Reject The Default Change
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer to keep omitted-option group kill and solve only specific caller paths.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup After Rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, preserve current-main behavior, and land the leader-check approach once focused tests and CI are clean.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper and overlapping process-runtime files are recently carried forward in the agent-core move under this history, so this is the best available owner for the rebase and shared-helper tradeoff.
